title: Stream-splitting and finalization heuristics for delayed outputs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Fixes and hardens how the metering pipeline accounts for streaming responses that are split across multiple fragments, possibly arriving out of order or with delayed finalization signals. This ticket focuses on heuristics to decide when to emit final token credits to customer ledgers vs. keeping provisional credits while waiting for terminal frames ("finalization watermark").
background: We observed several customer incidents where partial streaming fragments were charged immediately and then later retracted, leading to ghost charges or duplicate credit corrections. Root causes include intermittent network reconnects, model fallback mid-stream, and delayed terminal frames from the serving runtime after speculative decoding. Current pipeline assigns final credits on receipt of a terminal frame, but many clients and proxies cause final frames to be delayed or replayed, creating reconciliation churn in the billing ledger.
proposed_solution: Introduce a bounded finalization watermark with adaptive hold time: 1) when a non-terminal fragment arrives, emit provisional credits marked provisional:true in the interim ledger; 2) hold finalization for up to X ms (adaptive based on recent stream latency percentiles); 3) on terminal frame, atomically convert provisional credits to final; 4) if watermark expires, finalize conservatively (prorate speculative tokens) and emit a reconciliation entry. Add idempotency anchors for fragment streams and a replay-resume protocol to avoid double-crediting. Update rate-limiter interaction to treat provisional credits as soft quota reservations, not hard consumption.
acceptance_criteria: Provisional credits are recorded and visible in billing dashboard with provisional tag
Finalization watermark defaults to 250ms and uses P95 stream latency for adaptive extension
No duplicate final credits in synthetic test harness across 10k randomized reconnect scenarios
Reconciliation entries created for expired watermarks and tie to original stream id
Rate limiter treats provisional credits as reservations and prevents hard quota exhaustion during provisional window
tasks: Design data model changes for provisional vs final credit rows (billing ledger column additions)
Implement watermark manager in metering-ingest service and expose adaptive config
Add idempotency anchors to stream fragment envelope (server + client token) and enforce dedupe in aggregator
Integrate provisional-reservation semantics with quota service and rate limiter
Add e2e tests in metering-harness with network partitions, reconnects, mid-stream model switch, and speculative decodes
Create Grafana panel for provisional vs final credit counts and reconciliation churn
Write migration script to backfill provisional flag for recent incidents (opt-in via feature flag)
Docs: update SDK streaming contract and public FAQ about potential provisional credits
risk_and_tradeoffs: Holding credits longer reduces ghost-charge churn but increases complexity and transient ledger states. Conservative finalization may underbill short-lived speculative tokens; aggressive finalization may cause more retractions and customer confusion. Adaptive watermark uses observed latencies but adds operational tuning. The provisional-reservation model requires quota service changes which risk race conditions; mitigations include optimistic locking and reconcile jobs.
